examples.en: Before sunrise, the dawn sky looks bluish.
After swimming for a long time, my lips turned bluish.
A bluish light comes into the room.
The photo came out bluish, so I took it again.
The lake in the moonlight looks so faintly blue.
The early morning mist was bluish and mysterious.

explain: 완전한 파란색이 아니라 연하게 푸른빛이 도는 색이에요. 새벽 하늘, 달빛, 추워서 변한 입술처럼 '살짝 푸르게 보이는' 때 써요. 비슷한 '파르스름하다'는 좀 더 맑고 연한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Bluish moonlight came through the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸밀 때는 '푸르스름한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 푸르스름한 to describe a noun.

phrases.en: My face turned bluish from the cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 변하는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a color change.

phrases.en: The morning sky is a pale blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 푸르스름하다보다 더 맑고 연한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter and clearer than 푸르스름하다.

explain_en: It describes a color that is faintly blue rather than fully blue. Use it for things that look slightly blue, like dawn skies, moonlight or cold lips. The similar '파르스름하다' feels a bit lighter and clearer.

examples.en: Sunflowers have bloomed fully in the field.
Sunflowers bloom with yellow flowers in summer.
My grandmother shelled sunflower seeds for me.

examples.ko: 여름 여행 때 해바라기 밭에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: On my summer trip I took pictures in a sunflower field.
I hung a sunflower painting by the window.
I looked up at the tall sunflower.

explain: 해를 따라 움직이는 모습에서 생긴 이름이에요. 노란 꽃잎이 크고 둥글어서 여름 꽃의 대표로 꼽혀요. 꽃이 지고 나면 먹는 씨앗이 남는데, 이것을 '해바라기씨'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I eat sunflower seeds as a snack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해바라기에서 나오는 먹는 씨앗이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The edible seeds from a sunflower.

phrases.en: In summer I took photos in a sunflower field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해바라기가 많이 핀 넓은 땅을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A wide field full of blooming sunflowers.

phrases.en: Sunflowers bloom facing the sun.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해바라기'와 같은 뜻이고, 꽃임을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same as '해바라기', used to make clear it is the flower.

explain_en: The name comes from how the flower seems to follow the sun. Its big, round yellow petals make it a symbol of summer flowers. After it fades, the edible seeds are called '해바라기씨'.

examples.ko: 저는 비행기 공포증이 있어서 해외여행을 못 가요.
examples.en: I have a fear of flying, so I can't travel abroad.

examples.ko: 동생은 개 공포증이 있어서 산책을 싫어해요.
examples.en: My younger brother has a fear of dogs, so he dislikes walks.

examples.ko: 그는 공포증을 이기려고 상담을 받고 있어요.
examples.en: He is getting counseling to overcome his phobia.
My hands shake because of my fear of presenting.

examples.ko: 공포증은 노력하면 조금씩 나아질 수 있어요.
examples.en: A phobia can improve little by little with effort.
Many people have a fear of elevators.

explain: '무섭다'는 그때그때의 느낌이고, '공포증'은 특정한 것을 지나치게 무서워하는 상태예요. '고소공포증', '폐쇄공포증'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여 한 단어로 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 고소공포증이 있어서 높은 곳이 무서워요.
phrases.en: I have a fear of heights, so high places scare me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 곳을 지나치게 무서워하는 공포증이에요. 앞에 대상을 붙인 한 단어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phobia of high places. The object comes before 공포증 as one word.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has a phobia of bugs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무서워요'보다 오래 가는 심한 두려움을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a lasting, strong fear, more than just 무서워요.

phrases.en: I practice a little every day to overcome my phobia.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공포증을 이겨 내는 과정을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about the process of overcoming a phobia.

explain_en: 무섭다 is a feeling in the moment, while 공포증 is a condition of excessive fear of a specific thing. The target is attached in front as one word, like 고소공포증 or 폐쇄공포증.

examples.en: The kids are giggling while watching a cartoon.

examples.ko: 친구들과 깔깔거리다 보니 시간이 훌쩍 갔어요.
examples.en: While laughing with my friends, the time just flew by.
The sound of loud laughter woke me up.
You must not guffaw in the library.
My sister burst out laughing even at trivial things.
Don't just stand there laughing, help me a bit.

explain: '깔깔'에 '-거리다'가 붙어 소리 내어 웃는 행동이 계속된다는 뜻이에요. '깔깔대다'와 거의 같은 뜻이라서 바꿔 써도 돼요.

phrases.en: Everyone guffawed while watching the movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깔깔거리다'의 과거형이라서 이미 있었던 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the past tense, used for something that already happened.

phrases.en: Please don't guffaw in the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 웃지 말라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 쓰는 존댓말 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask someone not to laugh loudly.

phrases.en: I took photos while giggling loudly with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깔깔거리다'와 뜻이 거의 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as '깔깔거리다', so the two can be swapped.

explain_en: Bright, shrill, repeated laughter, usually of young people; interchangeable with (깔깔대다). '-거리다' is added to '깔깔' to show that the loud laughing keeps going. It means almost the same as '깔깔대다', so the two can be swapped.

t90.ax: You must not guffaw in the library.

en: to marvel at; to be amazed

examples.en: The children are amazed when they see the magic trick.
Everyone was amazed at his singing skills.
My parents were amazed at my Korean skills too.

examples.ko: 선물을 받고 놀라워하는 친구의 얼굴이 기억나요.
examples.en: I remember my friend's amazed face when she got the gift.

examples.ko: 사람들은 새 건물을 보고 놀라워하고 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: People were amazed at the new building and took pictures.
Your teacher will be amazed when she hears the result.

explain: '놀랍다'는 내가 느끼는 마음이고, '놀라워하다'는 그렇게 느끼는 모습을 겉으로 보이는 거예요. 그래서 '친구가 놀라워해요'처럼 다른 사람 이야기에 잘 어울려요. 갑자기 깜짝 하는 것은 '놀라다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: He looked at the present with an amazed face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -는 to describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: Don't be too amazed, it's okay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 부정 명령을 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle negative request to someone.

phrases.en: He clapped while looking amazed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라는 모습과 다른 행동을 같이 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say two actions happen at the same time.

explain_en: '놀랍다' is the feeling you have inside, while 놀라워하다 shows that feeling on the outside. That is why it fits well with another person's reaction, like '친구가 놀라워해요'. A sudden jump of surprise is '놀라다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling gets shy in front of strangers.
The child could not even say hello and was shy.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 칭찬을 받으면 수줍어하며 웃어요.
examples.en: That friend smiles shyly when praised.
Why are you so shy? Please speak freely.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 자리라서 다들 조금 수줍어했어요.
examples.en: It was a first meeting, so everyone was a little shy.

examples.ko: 수줍어하지 말고 앞에 나와서 노래해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't be shy, come to the front and sing.

explain: '수줍다'는 형용사이고, '수줍어하다'는 다른 사람이 수줍어하는 모습을 보고 말할 때 자주 써요. '부끄러워하다'는 잘못해서도 쓰지만, 수줍어하다는 낯을 가리거나 쑥스러운 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The shy child said hello quietly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수줍어하는 사람을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person who acts shy.

phrases.en: That friend said their name shyly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수줍은 모습으로 다른 행동을 할 때 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to link a shy manner to another action.

phrases.example: 여기서는 수줍어하지 마세요. 편하게 말해도 돼요.
phrases.en: Don't be shy here. You can speak freely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 부끄러워하지 말라고 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle way to tell someone not to be shy.

explain_en: '수줍다' is an adjective, while '수줍어하다' is often used when you describe someone's shy behavior. '부끄러워하다' can also be used for shame over a mistake, but 수줍어하다 means feeling bashful or self-conscious around others.

t90.ax: That friend smiles shyly when praised.

examples.en: The kids are beaming because they are going on a picnic.
It's payday, so Dad has been beaming since morning.
She beamed after receiving the gift.
Why are you beaming since this morning?
You came in with a beaming face, so I knew everything.
She did well on the exam, so she will be beaming.

explain: '싱글거리다'보다 기분이 좋아서 계속 웃는 느낌이 더 강해요. '싱글벙글 웃다'처럼 부사로도 많이 써요. 아이, 가족, 친구처럼 가까운 사람의 밝은 표정을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is smiling happily after getting a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사처럼 '웃다'와 함께 써서 기분 좋은 모습을 그려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like an adverb with '웃다' to show a happy look.

phrases.en: She opened the gift with a beaming face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '얼굴'을 꾸며서 밝은 표정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies '얼굴' to describe a bright expression.

phrases.en: My friend was grinning alone, so I asked why.
phrases.nuance_ko: '싱글벙글하다'보다 가볍게 웃는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels lighter than '싱글벙글하다'.

explain_en: Compared with '싱글거리다', it more strongly suggests someone keeps smiling because they are happy. It is also very common as an adverb, as in '싱글벙글 웃다'. It suits the bright expression of kids, family or friends.

t90.ax: She beamed after receiving the gift.

en: to have an affection for; to become attached to

examples.ko: 이 동네에 오래 살다 보니 정들었어요.
examples.en: After living in this neighborhood a long time, I've grown attached to it.
It hurts to leave the home I've grown fond of.
Even three days with a puppy, and you get attached quickly.

examples.ko: 정들기 전에 헤어지는 게 나을 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes it's better to part before you get attached.
Once you're attached it's hard to part, so be careful.
I haven't grown attached to my new school yet.

explain: '정이 들다'를 줄인 말로 시간이 지나며 자연스럽게 마음이 가는 걸 말해요. '정든 고향'처럼 꾸미는 말로도 많이 쓰고, 반대 느낌은 '정떨어지다'예요.

phrases.example: 정든 고향을 떠나는 날 많이 울었어요.
phrases.en: I cried a lot on the day I left my beloved hometown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 말로 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to modify a noun.

phrases.en: As we worked together, I grew attached.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄이지 않은 원래 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full, unshortened form.

phrases.en: Once I get attached, I hate to part, so I worry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-면'으로 조건을 말하는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form using -면 for a condition.
phrases.en_equiv: once attached, it's hard to part

explain_en: It is a shortened '정이 들다' and describes affection that grows naturally over time. It also modifies nouns, as in '정든 고향' (a beloved hometown), and its opposite feeling is '정떨어지다'.

en: to excite; to arouse; to thrill

examples.en: The news got the fans very excited.
It was a performance that thrilled the audience.

examples.ko: 아이를 너무 흥분시키면 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: If you get a child too wound up, he can't sleep.
Don't wind up an angry person even more.
He spoke loudly and stirred people up.

examples.ko: 개를 흥분시킬 수 있으니 조용히 하세요.
examples.en: Be quiet, because you might get the dog worked up.

explain: 기분 좋은 쪽은 '신나게 하다'가 더 자연스러워요. '흥분시키다'는 사람이나 동물을 가라앉히기 어렵게 들뜨게 하거나 화나게 할 때 주로 써요. '너무 흥분시키지 마세요'처럼 조심하라는 말과 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: Please don't get the child too worked up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심하라는 뜻으로 가장 자주 듣는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, used as a warning.

phrases.en: That song got everyone excited.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분 좋은 쪽의 흥분은 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural for positive excitement.

phrases.en: The loud noise got the puppy worked up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흥분시키다'와 뜻이 같고, 조금 더 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 흥분시키다, said in a more spelled-out way.

explain_en: Causative; something makes others excited. For a pleasant mood '신나게 하다' sounds more natural. '흥분시키다' is mostly used when someone is made so worked up or angry that they are hard to calm down, whether a person or an animal. It often comes with a warning, as in '너무 흥분시키지 마세요'.

examples.en: The bottle's opening was narrow, so I used a funnel.

examples.ko: 기름을 부을 때는 깔때기가 있으면 편해요.
examples.en: It's easier when you have a funnel for pouring oil.

examples.ko: 깔때기 없이 부었더니 바닥에 다 흘렀어요.
examples.en: I poured it without a funnel and spilled it all over the floor.

examples.ko: 주방 서랍에서 작은 깔때기 좀 꺼내 주세요.
examples.en: Please take a small funnel out of the kitchen drawer.

examples.ko: 종이를 깔때기 모양으로 말아서 소금을 넣었어요.
examples.en: I rolled the paper into a funnel shape and poured in the salt.

examples.ko: 이 깔때기는 구멍이 작아서 물이 천천히 내려가요.
examples.en: This funnel has a small hole, so the water goes down slowly.

explain: 주방뿐 아니라 과학 실험이나 자동차에 기름을 넣을 때도 자주 나와요. 위는 넓고 아래는 좁은 모양을 말할 때 '깔때기 모양'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: An ice cream cone is funnel-shaped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위는 넓고 아래는 좁은 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a shape that is wide at the top and narrow at the bottom.

phrases.en: I slowly poured water into the funnel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깔때기를 쓸 때 '붓다'와 함께 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears together with '붓다' when using a funnel.

phrases.en: I put a funnel in the bottle and added oil.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 통 입구에 깔때기를 끼워 놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you set a funnel into the mouth of a bottle or container.

explain_en: It appears not only in the kitchen but also in science experiments and when putting oil into a car. People also say '깔때기 모양' for anything wide at the top and narrow at the bottom.

en: to stick to; to cling to

examples.en: The rice stuck to the pot, so it's hard to wash.
Gum got stuck to my shoe.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마한테 딱 들러붙어서 안 떨어져요.
examples.en: The child clings to the mom and won't let go.
It's uncomfortable when wet clothes cling to your body.

examples.ko: 파리가 음식에 들러붙지 않게 덮어 두세요.
examples.en: Cover the food so flies don't land and stay on it.
The egg is going to stick to the frying pan.

explain: 들러붙다는 '붙다'보다 끈적하게 꽉 붙어서 잘 안 떨어지는 느낌이 강해요. 사람에게 쓰면 계속 따라다니며 귀찮게 한다는 부정적인 뜻이 돼요. 활용은 규칙이라 '들러붙어요', '들러붙었어요'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Wet clothes cling to my body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 아주 비슷하고, 일상에서는 '달라붙다'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Very close in meaning; '달라붙다' is more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: Rice doesn't stick to this pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않아요'를 붙이면 안 붙는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-지 않아요' means it does not stick.

phrases.en: The gum is stuck on, so it's hard to remove.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하며 문장을 이어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give a reason and continue the sentence.

explain_en: Sticky thing clinging to a surface, or a person clinging to someone (껌이 들러붙다) 들러붙다 feels stickier and harder to pull off than plain '붙다'. Used about people it is negative, meaning to cling and keep bothering someone. It conjugates regularly: '들러붙어요', '들러붙었어요'.

examples.en: Cold wind comes in through the gap in the door.
My finger got caught in the door gap and it hurt.
The gap around the door is wide, so bugs come in.
Light leaked out through the crack in the door.
I sealed the door gap with tape, and it's less cold now.
I heard laughter through the crack in the door.

explain: 문과 문틀 사이처럼 좁게 벌어진 곳이에요. '문틈으로 엿보다', '문틈에 끼이다', '문틈으로 바람이 들어오다'처럼 짝지어 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The child peeked into the room through the gap in the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 열린 문 사이로 몰래 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when secretly looking through a slightly open door.
phrases.en_equiv: to peek through the door gap

phrases.en: My bag strap got caught in the door gap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이나 몸이 문 사이에 끼었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an object or body part gets caught in the door.
phrases.en_equiv: to get caught in the door gap

phrases.en: In winter, wind comes in through the gap in the door, so it's cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문이 꼭 닫히지 않아서 바람이 들어오는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes wind coming in because the door doesn't close tightly.
phrases.en_equiv: wind comes in through the door gap

explain_en: It is the narrow gap between a door and its frame. It pairs naturally with phrases like '문틈으로 엿보다' (peek through the crack), '문틈에 끼이다' (get caught in the gap) and '문틈으로 바람이 들어오다' (wind comes through).

examples.en: I took the Christmas decorations out of the box.
I made this ornament myself.
The ornaments hanging on the tree are sparkling.
I hung a small picture as a wall decoration.
Dust has piled up on the decorations.

examples.ko: 장식물 하나 때문에 방 분위기가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: The room's mood changed because of a single ornament.

explain: 꾸미기 위해 놓거나 다는 물건을 두루 가리켜요. '장식품'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 둘 다 집이나 행사 분위기를 꾸밀 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I put a small decoration in the living room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷한 말이고, 집 안에 두는 작은 물건에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, used more for small items kept at home.

phrases.en: I hung ornaments on the Christmas tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매달거나 붙여서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when decorating by hanging or attaching.

phrases.en: I use empty bottles as decorations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 용도가 다른 물건을 꾸미는 데 쓸 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an item with another purpose serves as decoration.

explain_en: It broadly refers to things placed or hung for decoration. '장식품' is used in a similar way, and both come up often when decorating a home or an event.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 문고리를 잡을 때 정전기가 자주 생겨요.
examples.en: In winter, static often builds up when I grab a door handle.

examples.ko: 스웨터를 벗었더니 머리카락이 정전기 때문에 곤두서요.
examples.en: I took off my sweater, and my hair stands up from the static.
I sprayed anti-static spray on my clothes.
My fingertip stung, so I thought it was static.
Static happens easily on dry days.

examples.ko: 차에서 내릴 때마다 정전기에 깜짝 놀라요.
examples.en: Every time I get out of the car, the static makes me jump.

explain: '정전기가 일어나다', '정전기가 생기다'처럼 써요. 건조한 겨울에 많이 느끼고, 그때의 따끔한 느낌은 '따끔하다'나 '찌릿하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Static electricity built up when I took off my clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정전기'와 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 'jeongjeongi'.

phrases.en: In winter I spray anti-static spray.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정전기를 막는 물건이나 방법에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach it to things or methods that prevent static.

phrases.example: 문고리를 잡았더니 정전기 때문에 손이 찌릿했어요.
phrases.en: When I grabbed the doorknob, my hand tingled from static.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정전기가 닿았을 때의 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes how static feels when it zaps you.

explain_en: You say 정전기가 일어나다 or 정전기가 생기다 for static building up. People notice it most in dry winter air, and the sting is described with 따끔하다 or 찌릿하다.

examples.en: The police officer blew a whistle and stopped the car.

examples.ko: 체육 선생님이 호루라기를 불자 모두 모였어요.
examples.en: When the gym teacher blew the whistle, everyone gathered.
I was startled by the sound of a whistle.

examples.ko: 등산할 때 위급하면 호루라기를 불어서 알려요.
examples.en: When hiking, if there's an emergency, blow a whistle to signal.

examples.ko: 목에 호루라기를 걸고 있는 사람이 심판이에요.
examples.en: The person with a whistle around his neck is the referee.

examples.ko: 호루라기가 고장 났는지 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: It doesn't make a sound, so the whistle may be broken.

explain: 도구로 부는 '호루라기'는 '불다'와 함께 써요. 입술로 내는 소리는 '휘파람'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 심판, 경찰, 선생님이 신호를 줄 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I can hear a whistle sound from the playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 말할 때 '호루라기 소리'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'horuragi sori' to talk about the sound.

phrases.example: 선생님은 항상 호루라기를 목에 걸고 계세요.
phrases.en: The teacher always wears a whistle around the neck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체육 선생님이나 경찰 모습을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe a PE teacher or police officer.
phrases.en_equiv: to wear a whistle around the neck

phrases.example: 심판이 호루라기로 경기 시작 신호를 줬어요.
phrases.en: The referee gave the start signal with a whistle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구로 신호를 보낼 때 '-(으)로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-(eu)ro' to show the whistle is the tool.

explain_en: Physical whistle tool used by teachers, referees, and police (호루라기를 불다) The device '호루라기' goes with the verb '불다' (blow). A whistle made with your lips is '휘파람', which is different. It often appears with referees, police, and teachers giving signals.

t90.ax: I was startled by the sound of a whistle.
